figures.caption: 圖：體育課的跳繩比賽
figures.description: 操場上的體育課正在舉行跳繩比賽。兩名學生分別站在左右兩端，用力搖著一條長長的大繩；中間有三個學生正一起跳過繩子；後面還有四、五個同學排隊，等著輪到自己上場；右邊一個女生拿著計數板大聲數數，板子上寫著 23，旁邊幾個同學舉起手臂替跳繩的人加油；體育老師站在後面，拿著碼錶計時。

questions.stem: 提示：體育課上，老師舉辦了一場班級跳繩比賽，同學們分組上場、互相加油。請仔細看下面的圖片，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段描述圖中的學生們在跳繩比賽中做些什麼；第二段寫出你自己參加過的一次體育課比賽或團體活動，並說明你喜歡或不喜歡這類比賽的原因。

1.explanation_zh: 這一題有三個要求：第一段描述跳繩比賽中各人的角色（搖繩、跳繩、排隊、數數加油、老師計時）；第二段寫一次自己參加過的體育課比賽或團體活動，再說明喜歡或不喜歡這類比賽的原因。經驗不一定要是跳繩，拔河、大隊接力都可以，但要寫出比賽中發生的具體事情。
evidence: 第一段描述圖中的學生們在跳繩比賽中做些什麼
寫出你自己參加過的一次體育課比賽或團體活動
1.strategy_zh: 第一段把每個人的「角色」寫出來：turning the rope、jumping、waiting、counting、cheering；第二段用 At first … Then … After that … 寫比賽經過，再接理由。
hints: 第一段：Two students are … In the middle, … On the right, …
第二段：Last …, my class joined a … contest. 接比賽的經過
說理由時可以兼顧優點與缺點，最後回到自己的看法

moves.zh: 描述圖中的學生們在跳繩比賽中做些什麼
寫出你自己參加過的一次體育課比賽或團體活動
說明你喜歡或不喜歡這類比賽的原因

content.focus_zh: 第一段寫出至少三種角色（搖繩、跳繩、數數加油等）；第二段要有一次具體的比賽經過，並說明喜歡或不喜歡這類比賽的理由。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 經驗依時間順序寫（一開始、後來、結果），理由放在經驗之後；兩段之間用「我也參加過…」自然轉接。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。
重點排列混亂，前後句常接不起來，讀者不容易跟上。
看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 圖片用現在進行式；比賽經過用過去式（kept losing、won）；so that 後面接完整子句。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。
幾乎沒有正確的句子，無法理解。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 跳繩、拔河、加油、輪流等說法（jump rope、tug-of-war、cheer for、wait for one’s turn）要用對；避免一直重複 happy 和 fun。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The picture shows a jump rope contest in a PE class. Two students are standing at the two ends of a long rope and turning it. In the middle, three students are jumping over the rope together. Behind them, four or five classmates are waiting in line for their turn. On the right, a girl is counting the jumps out loud, and several students are raising their arms to cheer for the jumpers. The PE teacher is standing behind them and keeping time with a watch.
Last semester, my class joined a tug-of-war contest in PE class. At first, our team kept losing because everyone pulled at different times. Then our class leader asked us to count out loud together so that we could pull at the same time. After that, we won three games in a row. I really enjoy this kind of contest because it teaches us to work as a team. For example, even students who are not good at sports can help their team win. However, some students may feel nervous or sad when they make mistakes. In short, team contests are fun and meaningful as long as we support one another.

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
Out on the sports field, the PE class in the picture has turned an ordinary lesson into a lively jump rope contest. At each end of a long rope, a student is swinging it in wide, steady circles, while three teammates are leaping over it side by side, their feet leaving the ground at exactly the same moment. Behind them, the next group is waiting in a tight line, each person studying the rhythm before rushing in. Nobody wants to be the one who stops the rope. To the right, a girl holding a counting board is shouting out every jump, and the classmates around her are raising their fists and cheering frantically as the number climbs. Standing a little apart, the teacher is keeping an eye on his stopwatch, ready to announce the winning team.
Watching this scene brings back memories of the jump rope contest my class held last spring. Our group of eight could manage only twenty-three jumps in our first practice, mostly because one quiet classmate kept tripping and then apologizing to everyone. Instead of blaming him, our captain deliberately moved him to the middle of the line and asked all of us to count aloud, so that he could follow our voices rather than watch the rope. That small change made a huge difference. Within two weeks, we reached sixty-one jumps and won second place. We could hardly believe it. Admittedly, contests like this can put heavy pressure on students who are not athletic, and they may easily feel overwhelmed by a careless comment. Even so, I enjoy these contests, since they show that a team's success depends less on its strongest member than on how well its members coordinate with one another. In the end, the real prize was not the certificate but the sight of that once-nervous classmate grinning as he landed the final jump.

notes.zh: 用動作與獨立分詞構句寫出默契

notes.text: To the right, a girl holding a counting board is shouting out every jump, and the classmates around her are raising their fists and cheering frantically as the number climbs.
Our group of eight could manage only twenty-three jumps in our first practice, mostly because one quiet classmate kept tripping and then apologizing to everyone.
Within two weeks, we reached sixty-one jumps and won second place.
In the end, the real prize was not the certificate but the sight of that once-nervous classmate grinning as he landed the final jump.
depends less on its strongest member than on how well its members coordinate with one another
notes.zh: depend less on A than on B：與其說靠 A，不如說靠 B

notes.text: not the certificate but the sight
notes.zh: not A but B：不是 A 而是 B

notes.text: their feet leaving the ground at exactly the same moment
notes.zh: 獨立分詞構句：補充說明

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 圖片描述把每個角色寫得生動，經驗段有數據、解決方法、讓步與見解，並從自己延伸到隊友（內容 5）；經驗依時間推進，結尾用一個畫面收束（組織 5）；獨立分詞構句、so that、depend less on…than on 等句型正確多樣（文法句構 5）；deliberately、overwhelmed 等字用得貼切，但整體以常用字為主（字彙拼字 4）。總分 19，屬頂標版。

top.comment_zh: 第一段寫出搖繩、跳繩、排隊、數數加油、老師計時等角色，畫面感強；第二段以一位常絆倒的同學為中心，依「第一次練習、隊長調整、兩週後的成績」的時間順序寫，讓步後提出「團隊靠協調而不是靠最強的人」的理由，結尾回扣那位同學，前後呼應。句構多變、用字精準，沒有語言錯誤。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段角色齊全；第二段拔河的經過依 At first／Then／After that 排列清楚，理由（學會團隊合作）明確，也提到可能的缺點。文法正確但句型較單純；「For example, even students who are not good at sports can help their team win.」不是具體例子而是一般敘述，For example 用得不太貼切。

issues_zh: （參考，不影響判定）字彙重點列的 tug-of-war、文法重點列的 kept losing／won 都來自範文內容，不是題目或圖會引出的字，建議規準改成通用敘述。

top.comment_zh: 第一段涵蓋搖繩、跳繩、排隊等待、數數加油與老師計時五種角色，並以細節營造緊張氣氛；第二段以隊友一再絆倒、隊長調整位置與數數口令的比賽經過為例，依時間順序寫出進步與結果，並承認壓力問題後回到喜歡這類比賽的理由與意義。文法、用字皆佳，未見錯誤。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段把搖繩、跳繩、排隊、數數加油與計時的角色寫齊；第二段的拔河經驗依 At first、Then、After that 排列，理由「學會團隊合作」清楚。文法無誤，用字大致精準（kept losing、in a row、cheer for）。例子「不擅長運動的人也能幫上忙」略為籠統，句型變化有限。
